parts:
Please review the formalization progress so far in smooth-poincare-4d/formalization. I'd like to make an initial version of an overall research plan within formalization/investigations. To this end, please read the manuscript in /papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/, and also review its sub-investigations, the file /papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/01_neck_geometry/brainstorm/notes, and the sibling investigation 02_dirac_and_twistor_spinors/01_dirac_collar_matching. 

I'd like to make a research plan within formalization/investigations that broadly follows the corresponding plan outline in the investigations I described. This will be the first version, so please make a research-overview, plan and progress folder directly within formalization/investigations, and number these versions so that they can be updated as the plan changes. Follow the guidance in FORMALIZATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW.  The goal right now is to formalize all of the building blocks leading up to the current research within the investigations that I pointed to, so that the collar / neck problem is verified to be the outstanding part of the problem, the goal is not currently to prove that part, which will be left for future research plans. 

Please create this formalization plan following the guidance above.

I’ll check what Lean has already verified, then trace the manuscript arguments to the collar hypotheses they use. I’ll use that dependency map to write the first overview, plan, and progress register.

The pinned Lean build passes, and I rechecked the three-axis Weyl theorem and its axioms. The manuscripts also draw an important distinction for the plan. A no-neck estimate would exclude a nonflat bubble under the stated smooth comparison hypotheses. It would still leave open how to enter that regime on an arbitrary homotopy sphere and how to handle a positive closed critical value.

The plan now has three distinct conclusions to check: exclusion of a nonflat bubble after complete accounting, recognition of the exterior after a controlled cut, and a chiral curvature bound from matched spinors. I’ve also written a first Lean target that isolates the finite energy contradiction, so it can be checked before the geometric infrastructure is ready.

The collar investigations added new derivations during this review. One gives a stronger single-cut target: a supplied nonflat smooth ALE core can yield a lower-energy class on the original smooth type without requiring an energy identity for the whole neck. I’ll include that target and identify the exact working notes behind it.

Created **Version 01** of the overall research plan in `formalization/investigations`. The overview, plan, and progress baseline are numbered so later editions can preserve what was known. One live register tracks tasks across editions.

[Research overview](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-overview/01_OVERVIEW.md) · [Research plan](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-plan/01_PLAN.md) · [Progress baseline](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-progress/01_BASELINE.md) · [Live register](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-progress/REGISTER.md)

The pinned Lean build passes. I rechecked the **three-axis Weyl identity and lower bound**, including their axioms. The flat Weyl and Bach symbols and the geometric chiral curvature projection remain open pilot tasks.

The plan traces three routes to distinct conclusions:

- **Full neck accounting** would exclude a nonflat bubble under the stated smooth comparison and coverage hypotheses.
- **One marked spherical cut** can yield a lower-energy competitor on the original smooth manifold when a full nonflat smooth ALE core is supplied. This route avoids the need for a whole-neck energy identity.
- **Dirac transmission** gives a chiral curvature bound once the matched fields satisfy a joint lower bound and a differentiated error estimate.

Version 01 leaves construction of the general collar to future research. Its final audit must identify exactly which geometric inputs each route still needs. For SPC4, the plan also tracks two independent global questions: entering the required energy regime on an arbitrary smooth homotopy sphere and resolving a surviving positive closed Bach-flat critical class.

The first proof task is the finite energy-accounting contradiction. It can begin before the geometric infrastructure is ready. This session’s transcript was unavailable for archival.

This is excellent. Can you make three numbered sub-investigations within the investigations folder for the different routes? Please also set them up in accordance with FORMALIZATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW, with their own respective research overviews, plans and progress files, that also link back to the broader files just set up.

I’ll check the existing pilot and the overall task register, then set up a formalization investigation for each route. I’ll link their plans back to Version 01 and give each proof task one clear owner.

I’ll keep the existing pilot as 01 and number the new routes 02–04. The full-accounting route will own the component estimates that the single-cut route also needs. Each route will have a bounded first task, with shared recognition theorems and the final audit staying in the parent program.

All three opening propositions type-check in the pinned Lean project, and the package build passes. The route registers mark their proofs as pending. I’ll now verify the links and check that every Version 01 task points to exactly one live owner.

Created three numbered formalization investigations after the existing `01` pilot. Each has its own research overview, plan, live progress register, and continuation prompt, with links back to Version 01.

| Investigation | First proof task |
| --- | --- |
| [02 · Full neck energy accounting](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/02_neck_energy_accounting/README.md) | Prove that finite energy accounting and a strict residual exclude a positive-energy bubble. |
| [03 · Single spherical cut and descent](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/03_single_cut_descent/README.md) | Prove the strict energy margin that puts the capped exterior below the recognition threshold. |
| [04 · Dirac transmission and chiral curvature](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/README.md) | Combine differentiated spinor estimates across a finite cover while retaining the energy of the uncovered region. |

The [parent register](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/research-progress/REGISTER.md) now directs each of the 39 original tasks to one live owner. The parent retains the shared recognition theorems, common collar conventions, and final audit. Construction of a general collar remains assigned to future research.

The pinned Lean build passes, and all three opening proposition types elaborate. Their proofs await activation. All links in the new and updated formalization files passed validation. The remaining repository-wide link warnings came from concurrent manuscript handoffs. This chat’s transcript was unavailable for archival.

Excellent. Can you write continuation prompts for all three investigations? These will be run with Astra on ultra. Please give the model broad authority to continue trying different routes, and to create helpers using Sol 6.2.

I’ll turn the three single-task handoffs into launch prompts for sustained Astra/ultra sessions. I’ll give each session authority to change proof strategies and use Sol 6.2 helpers, with clear ownership for files the sessions may touch in parallel.

Each prompt now gives Astra a concrete follow-on target after the opening lemma. I’ve also specified how the three sessions can share Lake and blueprint changes while each route keeps its own proof files and progress register.

Use one block per fresh **GPT-6.2 Astra** session with effort set to **ultra**. Each saved prompt authorizes Astra to try alternative proofs and Lean representations, revise tasks, create **Sol 6.2/ultra** helpers, and continue beyond the opening lemma.

**[02 · Full neck energy accounting](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/02_neck_energy_accounting/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md)**

```text
Activate sustained formalization of Route 02. Start with the finite accounting theorem and continue toward deriving the energy identity from geometric remainder estimates. Read and execute the launch prompt in:
/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/02_neck_energy_accounting/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md
```

**[03 · Single spherical cut and descent](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/03_single_cut_descent/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md)**

```text
Activate sustained formalization of Route 03. Start the strict exterior-energy estimate and the marked-boundary construction in parallel, then pursue descent on the original smooth manifold. Read and execute the launch prompt in:
/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/03_single_cut_descent/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md
```

**[04 · Dirac transmission and chiral curvature](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md)**

```text
Activate sustained formalization of Route 04. Start with the weighted finite-cover estimate and continue toward identifying which spinor transmission and differentiated-defect bounds control the residual curvature. Read and execute the launch prompt in:
/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md
```

All three can run concurrently. Route 02 coordinates shared Lake and blueprint edits unless a separate parent lead is already active. Each route maintains its own proof files and progress register.

This chat’s transcript was unavailable for archival.
